title: How to find all your paid subscriptions
dek: Search statements, billing platforms and receipts to trace recurring charges, identify who owns each plan, and catch annual renewals a short review misses.
metaDescription: Search statements, billing platforms and receipts to trace recurring charges, identify who owns each plan, and catch annual renewals a short review misses.

paragraphs: To find your paid subscriptions, review every payment account across a full year where possible, then cross-check app-store subscriptions, payment-wallet agreements and receipts. Match each charge to a service and billing account. No single app-store list or statement search guarantees that you have found everything.

A charge can show the store or payment processor rather than the service you remember joining. An annual plan may appear only once. Treat the first pass as discovery, not an instruction to cancel every recurring payment. This guide helps build the list; ending an unwanted contract is a separate step.

body.heading: Run a search with a visible boundary
items: List the bank accounts, current and replaced cards, wallets and household billing accounts you are authorized to review. Mark any missing statement periods.
Review roughly twelve months where available. Look for repeating merchants, variable recurring amounts and single charges that may be annual renewals.
Check Apple subscriptions under each relevant Apple Account. On iPhone, Settings, your name, then Subscriptions is the current documented starting point.
Check Google Play subscriptions under the Google Account that made the purchase. Repeat for other accounts you use; a direct website subscription may not appear.
Review PayPal automatic payments and saved businesses, plus other payment services, phone bills or platform memberships you actually use.
Search your receipts and renewal messages for subscription, invoice, membership, trial, renewal and the unexplained statement wording.
Record the service, billing owner, actual amount and cycle, next known charge, and evidence. Mark uncertain matches unresolved rather than guessing.

body.heading: Find the billing owner before making changes
paragraphs: [Apple's instructions](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118428) explain where device subscriptions are managed and what to do when an item is missing. [Google Play's guidance](https://support.google.com/googleplay/answer/7018481) says to use the account holding the subscription and notes that uninstalling an app does not cancel it. A familiar app icon is therefore not the same as a billing record.

[PayPal's automatic-payment guide](https://www.paypal.com/us/cshelp/article/what-is-an-automatic-payment-and-how-do-i-update-or-cancel-one-help240) directs website users to Settings, Payments, then Subscriptions and saved businesses or Automatic Payments. A saved payment arrangement does not by itself prove that a monthly charge is active. Cross-check actual merchant terms and recent transactions.

rows: Receipt names a video service and the owning account.

body.heading: Calculate the cost without hiding the next bill
paragraphs: For a monthly plan, multiplying the current price by twelve gives an annual equivalent, not a guaranteed future bill total. For an annual plan, dividing by twelve helps comparison but does not change the fact that the whole renewal may be taken on one day. Keep the real cycle and next known charge beside any normalized amount.

Do not add a PayPal entry and the bank's matching PayPal debit as two subscriptions. Conversely, do not merge two identical charges until you have checked whether they belong to separate accounts or genuinely duplicate services. Shared households should compare their own authorized records rather than using another person's login without permission.

body.heading: Unknown charges and decisions need different routes
paragraphs: If you recognize the service, decide keep, review or cancel. Check storage, exports, household access and contract terms before ending something that holds essential data. Use [the cancellation guide](/guides/how-to-cancel-subscriptions) when you have identified the actual billing owner. Save confirmation and check subsequent statements.

If a charge may be unauthorized, contact the bank or card issuer promptly through a verified channel and follow its dispute process. Do not spend days attempting to decode a suspicious merchant while an account remains at risk. Avoid giving credentials to a search service simply because it promises to find every subscription.

Finish by recording what the sweep covered and what it could not cover. Missing older records, other household accounts and longer billing cycles remain limitations. Add a reminder before known renewals and update the list when a new plan starts; do not call it complete forever.

items.q: Why is a subscription missing from my phone's list?
items.a: It may be billed directly by the provider, through another store, or under a different Apple or Google Account. Find the receipt and payment route rather than assuming it ended. Check only accounts you own or have permission to manage, and ask the relevant account holder to review their own list.

items.q: Will reviewing three months find annual plans?
items.a: It can miss them entirely. A longer statement history gives you a better chance of seeing annual charges, although even a year is not a guarantee. Search renewal emails and current account terms as well. Mark missing periods and unresolved leads so you know what remains outside the review.

items.q: Does cancelling an automatic payment cancel the service?
items.a: Not necessarily. Payment authorization and the underlying subscription contract are different things. Identify the billing owner and follow the service's cancellation procedure, then retain proof. If a charge is unauthorized, also contact your payment provider promptly rather than treating it only as an unwanted subscription.
